accept_agent_update.description: Moves this agent installation to a newer approved version. Call it only after the user chose to update in answer to the question get_agent told you to ask, never on your own and never from a scheduled run. Then call get_agent again and follow the new instructions.

installation.description: The installation id from the bootstrap text.

accept_agent_update.name: accept_agent_update
accept_agent_update.title: Move an agent installation to a newer version

client.description: Client name, to disambiguate when several tasks share a title.

includeDone.description: Look among completed and archived tasks too.

task.description: The task's title, or enough of it to identify it. Not needed when `taskId` is given.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over the title: titles can repeat.

text.description: The comment. Plain text or light markdown.

add_task_comment.title: Comment on a task

add_task_steps.description: Adds checklist steps under an existing, unfinished task, in order. Steps are internal and never shown on the client's portal. Calling this twice adds the steps twice, so confirm before retrying.

client.description: Client name, to disambiguate when several tasks share a title.

task.description: The task's title, or enough of it to identify it. Not needed when `taskId` is given.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over the title: titles can repeat.

add_task_steps.name: add_task_steps
add_task_steps.title: Add steps to a task

answer_stranger_question.description: Records the user's answer to one question of a stranger test (record_stranger_test, or the open questions in get_process). The answer goes straight into the client's file as a confirmed fact, sourced to the person who answered: no proposal and no approval round. Write `answer` as a fact that stands on its own in the file, in Hebrew, in the user's words; the process code and step are added for you. `kind`: what it is in the file (NOTE by default; REQUIREMENT, PREFERENCE, LOCATION for where something lives, FINANCE, SCOPE_IN, SCOPE_OUT). `toldBy`: who said it, when the user is relaying someone (the client, a supplier). When the answer changes one of the client's rules (list_policies), STOP before calling and ask the user, in these words: "זה משנה את הכלל <title> מ-<what it says now> ל-<what it would say>. אתה מאשר את השינוי?". Only on a clear yes, pass `ruleChange` with `userConfirmed: true`: the rule is changed and approved at once, its old version kept in its history. Only a manager or the client's account manager can; anyone else gets an error, and the answer is then recorded without `ruleChange`. On a no, record the answer without `ruleChange`. `notRelevant: true` closes a question that does not apply; nothing goes into the file.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

questionId.description: The question's id, from record_stranger_test or get_process.

newStatement.description: What the rule says from now on.

rule.description: The rule's id or its exact title, from list_policies.

userConfirmed.description: True only after the user said yes to the change, in this conversation.

answer_stranger_question.name: answer_stranger_question
answer_stranger_question.title: Record the answer to a stranger-test question

apply_task_plan_steps.description: Makes the steps of a task's current, approved work plan the task's checklist steps. Open steps that are not in the plan are removed; steps already done, and steps with time logged against them, are always kept and reported. Ask the user before calling it, and tell them that. Running it twice leaves the same steps.

client.description: Client name, to disambiguate when several tasks share a title.

task.description: The task's title, or enough of it to identify it. Not needed when `taskId` is given.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over the title: titles can repeat.

apply_task_plan_steps.name: apply_task_plan_steps
apply_task_plan_steps.title: Turn a plan into the task's steps

confirm_procedure_still_right.description: When get_process `staleReasons` says the approved document is out of date because the rhythm or one of the client's rules changed, and the steps still hold, this records that the approved version is still right ("המסמך עדיין נכון"), and the notice goes away. A contact who left as a step's approver is not cleared this way: the step needs a new approver (save_procedure_draft). Someone who approves the client's procedures, and only after they said the document is still right.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

process.description: The process code ("P3") or its title.

confirm_procedure_still_right.name: confirm_procedure_still_right
confirm_procedure_still_right.title: Say an approved procedure is still right

create_decision.description: Opens a decision on the client's portal: a question with two or three options, optionally Ankora's recommendation and an amount. Only the client's admin can answer it, and the answer is kept as a signed record. Nothing is sent to the client automatically - tell the user to let the client know. Optionally link it to a task and mark that task as waiting on the client until they answer. Calling this twice opens two decisions.

amount.description: The amount at stake overall, in shekels, when the decision is about money.

background.description: Short context the client needs to decide. Plain text.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

due.description: When an answer is needed, YYYY-MM-DD.

markTaskWaiting.description: With `task` or `taskId`: mark that task as waiting on the client. It clears by itself when the client answers.

amount.description: Cost of this option in shekels, when it has one.

detail.description: One line on what choosing it means.

label.description: The option, in a few words.

recommended.description: Ankora's recommendation. At most one option.

question.description: The question, in the client's language, as they will read it.

task.description: Title of an existing task on this client that this decision blocks.

taskId.description: The exact id of that task, when you have it (an Ankora prompt gives it). Preferred over `task`: titles can repeat.

create_decision.name: create_decision
create_decision.title: Ask the client to decide

create_process.description: Creates a new process in a client's file as a draft, or a work guide (kind GUIDE, "הוראת עבודה": how to do something, with steps and no rhythm or runs). Use it when the user asks to open one by hand; for what came out of a meeting or a document, propose_knowledge is the way, so a person reviews it. `sources` are codes from the client's source register (get_client_file) that say it; without them it enters as uncertain, with toResolve. Then set its rhythm (set_process_rhythm) and draft its steps (save_procedure_draft). Calling it twice creates two.

approvals.description: The approval thresholds, in words. Each step's own approver is set in its procedure.

backup.description: Who stands in for the owner, by name.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

exceptionPlaybook.description: What to do when it goes wrong.

executor.description: Who does it today: a person at Ankora or a contact in the client's file by name, or free words when neither ("Nextage").

externalParty.description: Who outside the client takes part (an accountant, a bank), in words.

owner.description: Who owns it: a person at Ankora on the client, by name.

purpose.description: What it is for, in one or two sentences.

rhythmNotes.description: Notes on when it runs that schedule nothing ("the file goes to Nextage two business days before").

sla.description: How long handling may take, in words.

toResolve.description: Without sources: what would confirm it.

create_process.name: create_process
create_process.title: Create a process or a work guide

create_task.description: Creates a new Ankora task on one client, optionally with its steps, a supervisor and portal visibility in the same call. The task is visible to everyone who works on that client; the client sees it on their portal only if `clientVisible` is true. Assigning it, or naming a supervisor, is allowed only for colleagues with access to that client; pass the name the user said and Ankora will refuse with the usable names if it does not match. Calling this twice creates two tasks, so confirm the title, client and owner with the user before retrying. Every task gets a category, because a timer cannot run on a task without one: when the user did not name a category, do not ask them for it - pass the one you judge fits best if you know this client's categories, or omit it and Ankora picks one from the task's wording and how similar work was filed. An automatic pick comes back with `categoryOptions`, the client's other categories and what each is for: if one of them clearly fits the work better, set it with update_task. The result includes the new task's `url` in the Ankora app (staff sign-in required, not for clients). After creating, always tell the user which category the task got (say it was chosen automatically when `categoryAutoPicked` is true, so they know they can change it, and say plainly when `categoryNote` calls it low confidence) and give them the `url`, quoted exactly.

assignTo.description: Colleague's name or email. Omit to leave it unassigned; pass the user's own name for themselves.

category.description: Category name: the one the user named, or the one you judge fits best. Never ask the user for it. Omit it and Ankora chooses one automatically and says which in `category`.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it. Ankora matches it and says so if it is unrecognised or ambiguous.

clientTitle.description: The title the client sees, in their language, when it should differ from the internal title. Only meaningful with clientVisible.

clientVisible.description: Show this task on the client's portal as a promise they can follow. Off by default: most internal work is not something the client needs to watch. A visible task cannot be closed later without an outcome sentence.

details.description: Everything a colleague needs to pick this up without asking: an address, a reference number, what was already tried. Markdown for emphasis, lists and links; no headings or tables. Omit when the title says it all.

due.description: Due date, YYYY-MM-DD. Treated as the end of that day in the user's timezone.

mappingTask.description: A mapping task: one that maps how the client works (systems, people, requests, rules), such as a handover's "מיפוי וצפייה" stage. What it learns is proposed to the client file before it closes, and closing reminds when it was not. A description with the handover's "שלב: מיפוי וצפייה" line marks it on its own.

priority.description: How urgent. Omit unless the user said so - NORMAL is the default and most work is ordinary.

requireApproval.description: Whether the supervisor must sign it off before it can close. Needs `supervisor`.

steps.description: Checklist steps to create under this task, in order, as one-line titles. Up to 15. Steps are internal and never shown on the portal.

supervisor.description: Colleague's name or email to watch over this task. Must have access to the client. Clients cannot be supervisors.

title.description: What needs to be done. One line, as a person would write it.

create_task.name: create_task
create_task.title: Open a task

create_time_entry.description: Creates a completed Ankora time entry for the signed-in employee - time they already spent, rather than a running timer. Times are the wall clock in Ankora's own timezone (Asia/Jerusalem), matching what the app's manual-entry form does. Calling this twice creates two entries, so confirm with the user before retrying. Entries more than a couple of days old need `backdateReason`. Time that overlaps an entry on another client is not recorded on the first call: Ankora says what it overlaps, and you must ask the user whether to record both in parallel (each client is billed the full time) and only then call again with confirmParallel: true. Two entries on the same client never overlap. For time against a task the category can be left out: it comes from the task, or is chosen for a task that has none (and saved on it). Tell the user which category was recorded.

backdateReason.description: Why this is being recorded late. Required for older entries; Ankora will say so if it is.

category.description: Category name, when the user named one. Leave it out for a task: the task's own category is used. Without a task it is required.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it. Ankora matches it and says so if it is unrecognised or ambiguous.

closedBankOverrideReason.description: Only for SUPER_ADMIN or ANKORA_ADMIN, and only after the user saw Ankora's warning about changing a closed hour bank and confirmed it: why the time must be recorded in the closed bank anyway. Recorded in the audit log.

confirmParallel.description: Set to true only after Ankora refused the entry because it overlaps an entry on another client, and the user explicitly agreed to record both in parallel. Never set it on a first attempt. It never lets two entries on the same client overlap.

date.description: The day the work happened, YYYY-MM-DD.

end.description: End time, 24-hour HH:MM. Must be after start.

intoOpenBank.description: Only after Ankora refused the entry because its time falls in a closed hour bank: true records it in the open one instead, starting the moment that one opened, with a line in the note saying when the work was done. Pass it only after the user agreed, or in a scheduled run with nobody to ask; then say so in the run's report.

note.description: What the work was, in a few words. Required unless `task` is given.

task.description: Title of an existing Ankora task this time belongs to, as the user referred to it.

create_time_entry.name: create_time_entry
create_time_entry.title: Record time already spent

decide_approval.description: Carries out the decision on one row from list_approvals, exactly as its button on the screen does: approving a task signs and closes it (rejecting sends it back to work), an exception is approved or rejected, a rule approved or removed, a procedure or a plan approved, a summary approved for the portal or discarded, a guide version approved or rejected, a process decision carried out, Ankora's own items confirmed. Pass `kind` and `id` exactly as list_approvals returned them. A row that is no longer waiting on the user is refused. Proposals to a client file are decided with decide_knowledge_proposals. Before calling, tell the user what the row is and what the decision will do, and call only after they said so: the decision is real and others see it.

appliedLessonIds.description: Approving a procedure: the ids of the row's `openLessons` this version covers, as the user said. They close as applied in this version; the rest stay open.

id.description: The row's id, from list_approvals. Never typed or guessed.

reason.description: Why, in a line. Required where the row says `needsReason` (rejecting an exception or a guide version); kept with the decision otherwise where the screen keeps one.

decide_approval.name: decide_approval
decide_approval.title: Approve or reject a row on my approvals

decide_knowledge_proposals.description: Decides proposals to a client file, each as its own button on the review card: "approve" puts it in the file, "reject" drops it (needs `reason`), "already_in_file" closes it against the item already there and adds its source (only for a proposal list_approvals shows with `alreadyInFile`, as the card offers it only then), "task" opens a task from it instead (assigned to the user, due in three business days). Pass `proposalId`s exactly as list_approvals or propose_knowledge returned them. A proposal marked `approveAlone` (it changes an item in the file, may be a duplicate, or was flagged) is approved only in a call of its own, after the user read it. Each proposal is decided separately: one that fails is reported and the rest go on. For an item under `enteredAutomatically`, "reviewed_ok" marks it right ("תקין") and "revert" takes it out of the file again ("ביטול"), as its buttons do; only the decisions its row lists are accepted. Approving a process proposal also approves the procedure it brought when the user approves procedures of that client (a manager, or its account manager), the client has no separation of duties, and the procedure passes every check against the client's rules; otherwise the process enters as a draft. Before calling, tell the user which proposals and what will happen, and call only after they said so. Its result explains the fields it carries in `fieldNotes`: read them before answering.

proposalIds.description: The proposals, by proposalId. Never typed or guessed.

reason.description: Why they are rejected, in a line. Required for reject.

decide_knowledge_proposals.name: decide_knowledge_proposals
decide_knowledge_proposals.title: Decide proposals to a client file

decide_vendor_check.description: Answers a `vendorCheck` that create_task, update_task or save_task_plan returned: the task looks like connecting a new vendor to the app or the service Ankora gives clients. Judge it first: when it is clearly not a vendor (a test, a code, a person, an internal screen, a library, marketing or Ankora's own back office), answer NOT_A_VENDOR yourself and tell the user in one line. When it plausibly is one, ask the user in their language, naming the vendor, and answer with their decision; OPEN_RUN only on the user's word. OPEN_RUN opens a P8 (new subprocessor) run on Ankora's internal file, named after the vendor and linked both ways with the task; if that vendor already has a run, the task is noted there instead. NOT_A_VENDOR records that it is not (marketing, sales and Ankora's own back office are out of P8's scope). Pass `vendor` when the check had none, or to correct the name. Nobody answering for a business day opens the run anyway. Give the user `runUrl` exactly.

decision.description: OPEN_RUN: it is a new vendor that will reach client data. NOT_A_VENDOR: it is not.

vendor.description: The vendor's name, when the check had none or had it wrong.

decide_vendor_check.name: decide_vendor_check
decide_vendor_check.title: Decide whether a task connects a new vendor (P8)

delete_time_entry.description: Deletes one of the signed-in employee's own finished time entries, as the delete button in the app does. Pass the entryId from list_my_time_entries or create_time_entry. Before calling, show the user the entry (client, date, times, note) and ask them to confirm the deletion. The entry stops counting toward the client's hours; Ankora keeps it in its audit history. Use update_time_entry instead when only the times or the note are wrong. A running timer is not deleted here: stop it with stop_timer, or discard it in the app.

closedBankOverrideReason.description: Only for SUPER_ADMIN or ANKORA_ADMIN, and only after the user saw Ankora's warning about changing a closed hour bank and confirmed it: why the entry must be deleted anyway. Recorded in the audit log.

entryId.description: The entry's id, from list_my_time_entries or create_time_entry. Never typed or guessed.

delete_time_entry.name: delete_time_entry
delete_time_entry.title: Delete one of my time entries

dismiss_pdf_upload.description: Marks a signed PDF from pendingPdfUploads as reviewed without recording it, when it cannot be recorded: the footer code is missing or wrong, there is no visible signature, it is the wrong file. Managers and admins only. Give the reason in a sentence; it goes on the onboarding or offboarding task as a comment so a person can follow up, usually with a new upload code. The document stays in the file. Use it only after looking at the document; when you are unsure, leave it pending and comment on the task instead.

reason.description: Why it is not recorded, in a sentence.

dismiss_pdf_upload.name: dismiss_pdf_upload
dismiss_pdf_upload.title: Dismiss an uploaded agreement PDF

follow_email_reply.description: Makes a task, or a step (its title in `task`), wait for a reply to an email the user sent: it is marked as waiting on `waitingOn`, and when someone other than the sender writes in that thread, Ankora lifts the wait and tells the user. With no reply by `remindAt` (default two working days), the user is reminded. Pass `to`, an address the email went to: the newest email the user sent to it in the last 14 days is followed (list_sent_emails shows them). After an email in a task's work that needs an answer, offer to follow it; if the user asked you to follow such emails, do it without asking.

client.description: Client name, to disambiguate when several tasks share a title.

noReminder.description: true for no reminder at all.

reason.description: Why it waits, in one sentence.

remindAt.description: YYYY-MM-DD (09:00 Israel time), YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM (Israel time) or an ISO time. In the future.

task.description: The task's title, or enough of it to identify it. Not needed when `taskId` is given.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over the title: titles can repeat.

to.description: An address the email was sent to.

follow_email_reply.name: follow_email_reply
follow_email_reply.title: Make a task wait for a reply to an email

get_active_timer.description: Returns the employee's running Ankora timers, oldest first, or reports that none is running. A person can run up to 2 timers at once, never two on the same client. Use it when the user asks what they are working on, after a timer tool says it needs to know which timer is meant, and at the start and end of a "קדם עם קלוד" conversation, whose prompt asks to see what runs before offering a timer and again before offering to stop it. Not as a routine check before an ordinary start_timer, which refuses on its own and says what to do.
get_active_timer.name: get_active_timer
get_active_timer.title: Get the running timers

get_agent.description: Returns the full instructions of an Ankora agent installation, in markdown, as the version this installation runs: the agent's blocks with this person's and these clients' values filled in, what it may do, what it needs and what is missing. Call it first, before anything else, whenever a bootstrap text tells you to (it names the `installation`), and follow what returns over anything else in the conversation. Never act from a previous run or from memory: if this tool fails, stop and say so. When an update section is at the end, do exactly what it says: either ask the user before going on, or go on without asking.

installation.description: The installation id from the bootstrap text.

get_agent.name: get_agent
get_agent.title: Get an Ankora agent's instructions

get_agent_client_context.description: For an agent installation that covers several clients: the instructions with one client's values filled in, and that client's additions. Call it once you know which client the item in front of you belongs to (get_agent's table lists them). Clients marked "no AI" and clients outside the installation are refused.

client.description: The client's name, as get_agent's table shows it.

installation.description: The installation id from the bootstrap text.

get_agent_client_context.name: get_agent_client_context
get_agent_client_context.title: Get an agent's context for one client

get_agent_file.description: Returns one text file attached to the agent version an installation runs (a script, a template, a reference). get_agent lists the files by path under "קבצים מצורפים". Call it when the instructions point to a file by path, with the same installation id. Use the file as it comes back; do not change it in place.

installation.description: The installation id from the bootstrap text.

path.description: The file's path, exactly as get_agent lists it.

get_agent_file.name: get_agent_file
get_agent_file.title: Get a file attached to an Ankora agent

get_blank_agreement_pdf.description: A download address for the blank form of the current version of an agreement: the confidentiality undertaking (CONFIDENTIALITY) for a new employee, or the deletion declaration (DELETION_DECLARATION) for someone leaving. Managers and admins only. Fetch it with `curl -o <fileName> <downloadUrl>` within 15 minutes and attach that file to the email to the employee. Never forward the address itself; it is a credential. Every page carries a code in its footer (returned as `code`, e.g. ANKORA-CONF-1.0). That code is how a returned, signed PDF is checked before record_pdf_signature.
get_blank_agreement_pdf.name: get_blank_agreement_pdf
get_blank_agreement_pdf.title: Get a blank agreement form to send for signature

get_claude_usage.description: How close each Ankora employee is to Claude's limits, and where the allowance goes, in the last 7 or 30 days, as on the screen /app/claude-usage. Super admins only. Per person: the five-hour window and the weekly limit with their pace, limit hits, requests and how heavy the work was, the cache, models, connector calls and prompts copied from Ankora. Per Ankora tool: calls, answer sizes, refusals, truncation, images and repeat reads. Also signs of waste and the heaviest single requests. Use it to say who is close to getting stuck and what to shrink. It holds no prompt or answer text, only sizes and counts. Its result explains the fields it carries in `fieldNotes`: read them before answering.
get_claude_usage.name: get_claude_usage
get_claude_usage.title: Get the team's Claude usage

get_client_brief.description: A one-page brief of a client's file: who they are, their preferences and requirements, the rules to follow, finance and approval rules, how to communicate with them, what is temporary, open questions and specific working rules in full; people, systems, suppliers and processes by name and id; the next dates; and every "do not tell" in one list. Use it for a short question or a short message. For a process, a supplier, a document or anything longer, read get_client_file. Same rules as the file: no contact details, nothing sensitive. To stay short it leaves out the source codes, the owners and the ids of text items; get_client_file has them.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

get_client_brief.name: get_client_brief
get_client_brief.title: Get client brief

get_client_changes.description: What changed in a client's file since a date: every item added or changed, as it is now and in its section, and what left the file (removed, replaced by a new version, retired). Use it when you read the file earlier in this conversation, or in a run that repeats (pass the time of the last run), instead of reading the whole file again. since: YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO time, at most 90 days back; omitted, the last 7 days.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD or ISO time. Default: 7 days ago.

get_client_changes.name: get_client_changes
get_client_changes.title: Get client file changes

get_client_communication.description: One item from list_client_communications, by its `id`: a WhatsApp conversation's messages, or a recorded call's transcript. A conversation comes oldest first: the latest `limit` messages (default 100, at most 300) in the window `since`..`before` (YYYY-MM-DD, Israel time; `before` is exclusive). `hasEarlier` says there are older ones: ask again with `before` set to the first message's day. Messages from Ankora's side say `fromAnkora`; a voice message carries its transcript when one was made; a message deleted in WhatsApp is kept and marked `deleted`. A reply carries `replyTo`: who wrote the message it answers (`from`: "Ankora", a name, or "unknown" when WhatsApp hid it) and the quoted text. A call returns its transcript once it is ready (the nightly run makes them). The same visibility as list_client_communications. Read-only.

before.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Conversation only: messages before this day.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

id.description: The `id` of a conversation or a call, from list_client_communications.

limit.description: Conversation only: how many messages. Default 100.

since.description: YYYY-MM-DD. Conversation only: messages from this day on.

get_client_communication.name: get_client_communication
get_client_communication.title: Read a client's WhatsApp conversation or recorded call

get_client_email.description: Reads one email, or a whole thread oldest first, from the client's connected mailbox: who, when, the text, and the attachments with their ids. Pass `emailId` or `threadId` from search_client_emails. A long thread is cut so one read stays reasonable; read a single email by its id for its full text. Read-only.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

mailbox.description: The mailbox address, only when the client has more than one connected. get_client_mailbox lists them.

get_client_email.name: get_client_email
get_client_email.title: Read an email or a thread in a client's mailbox

get_client_file.description: Returns a client's file as one Markdown document, in Ankora's standard order: identity and legal entities, scope, people, preferences, requirements, the client's rules (follow them; a proposed rule's interim rule applies until it is approved), systems and access, suppliers, processes (with each one's approved procedure, whether it runs and why not, how well it is documented, and its gaps), finance, communication, dates, temporary information, one-off decisions, open questions, items awaiting confirmation, recent updates, and the source legend. Lines not yet confirmed say so, with what would confirm them; sources appear as [S1 08:13]. Contact details and sensitive items are left out. Read it before working on a client you have not worked on in this conversation, and before drafting anything to the client or their suppliers. Read earlier in the conversation: get_client_changes says what changed since.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

get_client_file.name: get_client_file
get_client_file.title: Get client file

get_client_mailbox.description: The client's own mailboxes connected to Ankora (through Unipile), whether each is working, what it can do, and the addresses it can send from. Call it before working in a client's mailbox, or when another mailbox tool says the connection dropped. An empty list means none is connected: the account manager connects one on the client's connections screen in Ankora. Read-only.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

get_client_mailbox.name: get_client_mailbox
get_client_mailbox.title: Get a client's connected mailbox

get_client_onboarding.description: Where the setup of a new client stands: what was filled in each of its four steps, what is still missing before it can be activated, and the link to the setup screen. Without `client`, lists every client being set up. A client being set up is in no other tool until a person activates it. For managers only. Its result explains the fields it carries in `fieldNotes`: read them before answering.

get_extraction_brief.description: Everything an extraction run needs before reading a meeting: Ankora's approved extraction guidance (follow it), the user's clients with the email domains that identify their meetings and each client's own data-handling rules, and the Fireflies recordings already turned into proposals in the last 30 days (skip those). `communications` says how to extract from the stored WhatsApp conversations and recorded calls, and what of them was already read. A client's `dataHandlingRules` bind every item proposed for that client, on top of Ankora's guidance: what they do not allow is not proposed at all. A rule marked as an interim rule applies as written until its proposed rule is approved. Matching a meeting to a client: a participant from a CLIENT domain decides it. A PARTNER domain decides it only when that partner appears under one client; if it appears under several, decide from the title and content and say why in the batch note. A meeting about several clients is split: each item goes to its own client's batch. A meeting with no client participant and no client named is internal: skip it.

Also the previous packages with their closing balance. Every value is in whole minutes. `asOf` (YYYY-MM-DD) gives the state at the end of that day, Israel time: entries that started by then, adjustments that took effect by then. Without it, the figures match the screen now. `since` (YYYY-MM-DD) answers whether a new package was loaded from that day on, for a period report. Adjustments and their reasons are internal: managers get them under `internalOnly`, and they must never be copied into anything sent to the client.

Metadata only: no proposal text, reason, quote or rejection reason is returned, and clients appear as opaque keys (L1, L2...). Proposals of a client marked "בלי AI" are left out and only counted. Rows are the heavy part of this tool: answer from `groups` when they are enough, and narrow rows with `since` and `via`. Its result explains the fields it carries in `fieldNotes`: read them before answering.

install_agent.description: Creates an installation of an Ankora agent for the signed-in person and returns its bootstrap text: the only lines to put in the Claude project's instructions, the scheduled task's prompt or the first message of a persistent conversation. Pass the agent (its name as the user calls it, or its id), where it will run, and its clients by name (or allClients). Installation-level values go in `values`, by parameter key. Start with preview: true: it installs nothing and returns `ask` (must be answered: the clients, the schedule of a scheduled run, required values, and required values per client, marked with `client`), `optional` (values the user may give now) and `requirements` (connectors, skills and the rest the run needs). Before asking anything, look at the tools you have in this conversation: a connector in `requirements` you have tools for is connected, so say nothing about it; mention only the missing ones. Then ask the user every `ask` item and offer the `optional` ones in ONE message, with each value's `example` as its format. Call again without preview with all the answers: installation values in `values`, client values in `clientValues` by client name. They are saved in Ankora by this call; never send the user to a screen to type them.

Put the page address (uploadPageUrl) and the code as plain text in the email to that employee only, next to the blank form from get_blank_agreement_pdf, with the line 'כדי להעלות, נכנסים לכתובת הבאה ומקלידים את הקוד:' and the address alone on the next line, as https://www.ankora.co.il/upload. Never attach a Hebrew letter to the address (for example ל-www...): mail clients turn the whole word into a broken link. The address carries no secret, so it does not matter if the mail client wraps it. The code must not be a link, and must never go anywhere else: not in a task, a comment, a chat or any other message. It is a credential. Ask the employee to upload the signed PDF there rather than replying with it. Once uploaded, the document appears in get_employee_status under pendingPdfUploads; check it, then record_pdf_signature or dismiss_pdf_upload.

propose_knowledge.description: Sends proposed items for a client's file, from ONE source (a meeting, a document, an email thread). Nothing enters the file until a person approves it on Ankora's review screen, except AUTO. STATUS, on each item as `status`: CONFIRMED (the client or their supplier said or showed it explicitly), UNCERTAIN (said unclearly, or only by Ankora) or MISSING (needed, and we do not have it). With UNCERTAIN or MISSING add payload.toResolve: what would close it. Left out, HIGH confidence is CONFIRMED and anything else UNCERTAIN. Not used on NARRATIVE, DOMAIN, TASK, DATE or a QUESTION fact. FIELDS: each item's `payload` is described in the schema per target (payload.anyOf, titled by target), with every closed list. For example FACT.kind (SCOPE_IN, SCOPE_OUT, PREFERENCE, REQUIREMENT, LOCATION, FINANCE, TEMPORARY, ONE_OFF_DECISION, QUESTION, NOTE) and FACT.topic (COMMUNICATION, REPORTING, DOCUMENTS, AUTOMATION, ADMINS, PAYMENTS, SUPPLIERS, OTHER). A value outside a list drops that item, and the reply says where (items[0].payload.topic). Each item needs `reason` (one sentence: why it is true and where it was said) and `confidence` (the review screen orders by it), and should have `at` (minute in the recording, "08:13"). `quote` is optional and short, never from a topics-only source. SOURCE: `sourceCode` ("S3") for a source in the client's register (get_client_file lists it), or `newSource` to register one; it is registered only when at least one item is kept. A source is found again by firefliesId, gmailThreadId (EMAIL), callId or whatsapp (see get_extraction_brief), so sending it twice makes no second source. An email thread is a source only when it is this client's; quote only what the client or their supplier wrote. CHANGES: to change an item already in the file, action SUPERSEDE with `targetId` (the id after the item in get_client_file) and only the fields that change. When someone said otherwise and it is not clear who is right, CONTRADICT with its targetId: nothing is overwritten. Never propose a second item for something in the file: names vary between meetings ("Washington DOR" and "Washington Department of Revenue"), so look for one first. The reply's `possibleMatches` lists new items that may already exist; resend them as SUPERSEDE or leave them to the reviewer. NAMES (entityName, routeToNames, systemNames and the like) link to the item in the file with that name on approval; name only what is in the file or in the same batch. Every payload except NARRATIVE, DOMAIN, TASK and DATE may carry externalRefs, ownerName (the person at Ankora who keeps it right) and clientVisible (true only when it is the client's to see; never with sensitivity SENSITIVE or doNotDisclose). Fill interimStatement (APPROVAL_REQUIRED/THRESHOLD rules) and verification (AUTOMATED steps). Never include passwords, keys or card numbers: such an item is dropped and a task to change the secret opens. sensitivity SENSITIVE for medical, political or personal information. Leave out small talk, guesses and Ankora's own commercial terms. WHOSE MEETING: a participant from a client's domain decides. A meeting about several clients: each item its own `client`, with newSource. Not clear and nobody decides: pass the likely `client` and `uncertain` with all candidates; nothing enters a file until a person picks. AUTO: a new plain fact, contact, provider or entity read as HIGH, not sensitive or flagged, may enter on arrival (`enteredFile`): tell the user which, with the `result` links.

record_pdf_signature.description: Records that a staff member returned a signed agreement as a PDF: the confidentiality undertaking (CONFIDENTIALITY) or the deletion declaration (DELETION_DECLARATION). Managers and admins only. The documentId is usually one from pendingPdfUploads (get_employee_status): the employee uploaded it with their upload code and it is already filed on "Ankora פנימי". Otherwise file it there first with upload_document or start_document_upload. A document on any other client is refused. Record ONLY after checking two things yourself. First, the code in the footer of every page: read the document's text with read_document and find the Latin code, e.g. ANKORA-CONF-1.0 or ANKORA-DEL-1.0, which must match the current version (get_employee_status gives the version; get_blank_agreement_pdf gives the code). Use the code, not the Hebrew version line, because Hebrew comes out of a PDF's text reversed. Second, that a signature is visibly there (open the file itself when the text cannot show it). If either is unclear, do not record: add a comment on the task asking a person to check, and stop. signedAt is the date on the signature, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM in Israel time. signedName is the name as written on the PDF. Safe to repeat: if this PDF channel is already recorded for the same person, kind and version, the existing record comes back with alreadyRecorded: true and nothing new is written. Either way the uploaded document leaves pendingPdfUploads. When the confidentiality undertaking is now signed both in the app and as a PDF, the onboarding task's PDF step closes by itself; for a deletion declaration a note is added to the offboarding task.

record_stranger_test.description: The stranger test: could someone who has never done this process run it tomorrow, from what Ankora has written down? Before calling: read the process (get_process: steps, open lessons, the questions already answered), the client's file (get_client_file, or get_client_changes if read in this conversation), and the documents that matter (list_documents). Then walk every step as a stranger: what do I do, where, with what input, how do I know it is done, who do I ask. Wherever you would get stuck, that is a question. Do not ask what the file or the procedure already answers, and do not ask for documentation for its own sake: only what would stop or slow a real run. severity: BLOCKER (cannot go on without it), SLOWS (can go on, slowly or by asking), IMPROVES (nothing waits on it). askWho: ANKORA (the owner or the account manager knows) or CLIENT (only the client or their supplier knows). step: the step it is about, or omit for the process as a whole. The questions of the previous test that were not answered are replaced by these. After recording, ask the user the questions one at a time, BLOCKER first, and record each answer with answer_stranger_question.

save_agent_draft.description: Writes the draft of an Ankora agent's next version: its instruction blocks, parameters, requirements and action level. Use it to bring an existing prompt into Ankora (split it into blocks, turn what differs per client or per person into {{parameters}}, move dated change notes out of the text into `changeNote`) or to change an agent the user asked to change. Pass `agent` (its slug, from the agent's url) to change an existing agent, or `create` for a new one. Blocks, parameters and files you pass replace the draft's whole list; leave one out to keep it as it is. A text file the instructions use (a script, a template, a reference) goes in `files` with the path the instructions name. Block kinds, in reading order: role, scope, steps, rules, approvals, language, output, tools, schedule, live. A rule for one client only is a client addition: save it with save_agent_client_addition, not here. Mark a block `overridable` when a client addition may replace it. Write {{key}} where a parameter's value goes; every such key must be in `params`. This tool never approves. The approval is recorded in the signed-in user's name. Pass the full plan text in `plan` (light markdown: **bold** section labels and lists, no # headings, up to 20000 characters) and one short imperative line per numbered step in `steps` (up to 15). `baseVersion` is the version you read: 0 when the task had no plan. If someone saved a newer version meanwhile, nothing is saved and the result says so; read it with get_task_plan, show the user the difference, and ask before saving again. If the task has no steps at all, an approved plan's steps are added to it automatically on save (the result says so); only when it already has steps, ask before apply_task_plan_steps. An approved plan also moves an open task to in progress (`taskStarted` says so); a draft changes nothing. The plan itself is internal and never shown to the client.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it.

exceptionPlaybook.description: What to do when it goes wrong.

executor.description: Who does it today: a person at Ankora or a contact in the client's file by name, or free words when neither ("Nextage").

externalParty.description: Who outside the client takes part (an accountant, a bank), in words.

kind.description: Make it a work guide (GUIDE) or a process (PROCESS).

notApplicable.description: Documentation fields that do not apply to this process ("לא רלוונטי"): they stop counting as missing.

owner.description: Who owns it: a person at Ankora on the client, by name.

process.description: The process code ("P3") or its title.

purpose.description: What it is for, in one or two sentences.

rhythmNotes.description: Notes on when it runs that schedule nothing ("the file goes to Nextage two business days before").

sla.description: How long handling may take, in words.

update_task.description: Changes an existing Ankora task: its status, owner, supervisor, due date, title, category, portal visibility or what it is waiting on. Identify the task by its title; if two tasks share one, Ankora will say so rather than guess. Only the fields you pass are changed - omitting a field leaves it alone. Use `clearAssignee` or `clearDue` to empty a field rather than passing an empty string. Finishing a task the client can see also needs `outcome`, one sentence in their language saying what came of it; Ankora refuses the close without it, because that sentence is what the client reads on their portal. A task that still has no category gets one chosen automatically with any change (a timer cannot run without it). Its result explains the fields it carries in `fieldNotes`: read them before answering.

assignTo.description: Colleague's name or email to hand it to.

category.description: New category for the task. Omit to keep the current one; a task with none gets one chosen automatically.

clearAssignee.description: Remove the current owner, leaving it unassigned.

clearSupervisor.description: Remove the supervisor. Also switches off any approval requirement, since nobody would be left to give it.

clearWaiting.description: The task is no longer waiting on anyone.

client.description: Client name, to disambiguate when several tasks share a title.

clientRequest.description: What we ask the client to do, as one sentence addressed to them: what, where and how long it takes. Shown on their portal under 'waiting for you' while the task waits on the client. Pass an empty string to clear it.

clientTitle.description: The title the client sees on their portal. Pass an empty string to fall back to the internal title.

clientVisible.description: Show (true) or hide (false) this task on the client's portal. Making a finished task visible needs an outcome sentence.

details.description: Replace the task's details with this. Markdown for emphasis, lists and links. Pass an empty string to clear them.

includeDone.description: Look among completed and archived tasks too - needed to reopen something already finished.

mappingTask.description: A mapping task: one that maps how the client works (systems, people, requests, rules), such as a handover's "מיפוי וצפייה" stage. What it learns is proposed to the client file before it closes, and closing reminds when it was not. A description with the handover's "שלב: מיפוי וצפייה" line marks it on its own.

outcome.description: One sentence, in the client's own language, saying what actually came of this. Required to finish a task the client can see - Ankora refuses DONE without it. Write what happened, not what it was called: the client reads this on their portal and it goes into their monthly summary.

requireApproval.description: Whether this task needs the supervisor's sign-off before it can be finished. Turning it on needs a supervisor. Once the task is waiting for approval, only the supervisor may switch it off.

status.description: New status. PENDING_APPROVAL means the work is finished and waiting for the supervisor to sign it off; DONE means finished; ARCHIVED means dropped without being done. A task that requires approval reaches DONE only from PENDING_APPROVAL, and only its supervisor may make that move.

supervisor.description: Colleague's name or email to watch over this task. A supervisor alone only watches; set `requireApproval` as well if they have to agree before it closes.

task.description: The task's title, or enough of it to identify it. Not needed when `taskId` is given.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over the title: titles can repeat.

title.description: New title, replacing the old one.

waitingOn.description: Mark the task as blocked, waiting on someone. CLIENT shows on the client's portal as 'waiting for you', so use it only when the client themselves has to act. Cannot be set on a finished task.

waitingReason.description: What exactly is being waited for, in one line. Only with waitingOn. Internal: never shown to the client.

update_time_entry.description: Changes one of the signed-in employee's own finished time entries: its times, note, category or task. Pass the entryId from list_my_time_entries or create_time_entry, and only the fields that change. To change the times pass date, start and end together, as the wall clock in Asia/Jerusalem. Confirm the change with the user before calling. Ankora applies the same rules as the app's edit form: an employee can change their own entry only within 48 hours of its start, and time that overlaps an entry on another client is not saved on the first call: ask the user whether to keep both in parallel, and only then call again with confirmParallel: true. A running timer is changed with update_timer_note or stop_timer, not here.

category.description: New category name, when the user wants a different one. Leave it out to keep the current one.

closedBankOverrideReason.description: Only for SUPER_ADMIN or ANKORA_ADMIN, and only after the user saw Ankora's warning about changing a closed hour bank and confirmed it: why the entry must change anyway. Recorded in the audit log.

confirmParallel.description: Set to true only after Ankora refused the change because the new times overlap an entry on another client, and the user explicitly agreed to keep both in parallel. Never on a first attempt.

date.description: The day of the corrected times, YYYY-MM-DD. Pass with start and end.

end.description: Corrected end time, 24-hour HH:MM. Must be after start. Pass with date and start.

entryId.description: The entry's id, from list_my_time_entries or create_time_entry. Never typed or guessed.

note.description: The new note. Replaces the existing one entirely.

reason.description: Why the entry is being corrected, in a few words. Saved in the entry's history.

start.description: Corrected start time, 24-hour HH:MM. Pass with date and end.

task.description: Title of an existing task on the same client to link this time to, as the user referred to it.

update_time_entry.title: Correct one of my time entries

update_timer_note.description: Replaces the note on one of the signed-in employee's running timers, without stopping it. Use this when the user says what they are working on while the clock is already going. With two timers running, pass the client of the one the note is for.

client.description: Client of the timer the note is for, as the user said it. Required only when more than one timer is running.

note.description: The new note. Replaces the existing one entirely.

update_timer_note.title: Update the running timer's note

upload_document.description: Files a document in a client's file in Ankora, optionally on a task, with the file's bytes inline as base64. Up to 1MB. If you can run commands (curl), prefer start_document_upload: it takes files up to 4MB and costs no tokens for the bytes. Use this one when you cannot. The document is hidden from the client unless `clientVisible: true`. Calling this twice files two documents, so confirm the title and destination with the user first.

client.description: Client name, as the user said it. Not needed when the task is given.

clientVisible.description: Show the document to the client in their portal. Default false. Pass true only when the user explicitly asked for the client to see it.

contentBase64.description: The whole file, base64-encoded, unchanged. A data: URL prefix is accepted.

fileName.description: The file's name with its extension, e.g. 'contract-signed.pdf'. The extension decides how the file opens.

kind.description: POLICY (an insurance policy), PROCEDURE (a procedure or process Ankora wrote), CERTIFICATE, CONTRACT, INVOICE or OTHER. Default OTHER.

mimeType.description: Only if you know it for certain. Otherwise omit; Ankora decides from the extension.

task.description: Title of the task the document belongs to, when it belongs to one.

taskId.description: The task's exact id, when you have it (an Ankora prompt or an earlier tool result gives it). Preferred over `task`.

title.description: The document's name as people will read it in Ankora, in Hebrew when the user writes Hebrew. Example: 'חוזה העסקה חתום - דנה כהן'.
